speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature of your dizziness—is it a spinning sensation (vertigo) or more of a lightheadedness? Also, how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these episodes last for less than a minute, and do they trigger any involuntary eye movements or nausea? I also need to know if the dizziness is consistently triggered by specific head movements, such as looking up or rolling over in bed.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: To confirm the diagnosis of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo, I will perform a physical exam to check for nystagmus during head position changes. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirms your diagnosis of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), which explains your position-dependent vertigo. I will now perform the Epley maneuver to reposition the displaced inner ear crystals and relieve your symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No history of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, or labyrinthitis. Social history: Retired school teacher. Lives alone. Non-smoker, occasional wine. Enjoys light gardening.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your age and history of living alone, it is crucial to ensure you have a safe environment to prevent falls while your vertigo resolves. I will prescribe the Epley maneuver for home practice and recommend using a cane or walker until the symptoms subside.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
